evidence.quote: Following the homogenization treatment, the alloys were hot rolled at 1000°C with a 68% thickness reduction. To ensure nearly isothermal hot deformation, the specimens were heated at 1000°C for 15 min before the first and for 5 min before each subsequent rolling pass.
After hot rolling, the samples were annealed at 1000°C for 5 min, followed by water quenching.
Further grain refinement of the alloys was achieved through cold-rolling at room temperature with a thickness reduction of 68%
followed by recrystallization annealing at 900°C in a vacuum for 7 min, followed by water quenching.

The XRD patterns of the Co20 and Co50 alloys after cold rolling and annealing at 900°C for 7 min are presented in Fig. 5. The results demonstrate that the cold-rolled and annealed samples of Co20 alloy consist of a single FCC phase. On the other hand, the XRD patterns of the cold-rolled and annealed Co50 alloy indicate the presence of a weak peak at 2θ = 47.64°, corresponding to the (1011) plane of the ε-martensite phase in addition to the FCC peaks.
The volume percent of the HCP phase (6%) in the annealed sample is lower than that of the as-cold rolled sample (27%), which can be due to the low stability of the HCP phase at higher temperatures.

The enhancement in ultimate tensile strength and ductility is attributed to the TWIP-TRIP effects during the tensile deformation of the Co50Cr20Ni20Fe5Mn5 HEA.
The principal strengthening mechanisms contributing to the increased yield strength with higher Co concentration were identified as initial HCP phase strengthening and grain boundary strengthening.

Furthermore, Co50 HEA exhibits a TWIP + TRIP effect during tensile deformation, resulting in increased ductility.
Initial HCP phase strengthening and grain boundary strengthening were identified as the primary strengthening processes leading to improved yield strength with greater Co content.
